candidates.spoken: One dead star spins 716 times a second.
What If Earth Spun Like the Fastest Pulsar?
Its equator moves at about 24% of light speed.
Earth spinning that fast would fly apart instantly.
Earth spun as fast as the fastest known pulsar.
PSR J1748−2446ad is the fastest-spinning pulsar known.
It's a neutron star under 16 kilometres in radius.
It sits about 18,000 light-years away, in Terzan 5.
Only a neutron star's gravity can hold such spin together.
Spin that fast isn't possible for ordinary planets.
It would not all happen at once.

script.spoken: One dead star spins 716 times a second. Its equator moves at about 24% of light speed. That's over 70,000 kilometres per second. It's a neutron star under 16 kilometres in radius. It sits about 18,000 light-years away, in Terzan 5. Earth spinning that fast would fly apart instantly. Only a neutron star's gravity can hold such spin together. So the fastest spinners in the universe are also the densest.
